title: Weight-Space Audit of MIT-p50c and DNA Weight Editing (SGNE-CC) on Qwen3.5-0.8B at a 32,768-Token Generation Limit (EN / RU)
read_level: full English paper (01_..._EN.md) and overview/manifest (00_...md); Russian version, figures (PNG) and reproducibility zip not opened
metadata_mismatch: corpus id is the concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24235217; Zenodo API resolves to version record 24235218 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24235218). EN paper heading omits 'on Qwen3.5-0.8B' and '(EN / RU)' from the record title. Corpus abstract was empty.
why_wsp: Audits the weight geometry of the MIT-p50c WSP edit (from Takehi et al.) on Qwen3.5-0.8B and compares it with SGNE-CC, a gradient-free norm-preserving column-rotation weight patch by the author; the procedure that produced SGNE-CC is not released and no LLM editor is named.
domain: LLM reasoning-loop repair (math, logic, code, multilingual text) on Qwen3.5-0.8B
editor: not stated for SGNE-CC ("The rotation-angle search procedure is not released"); MIT-p50c edit from Takehi et al. 2026 (GPT-6 Astra per that blog)
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B ("752M text parameters, 18 recurrent GatedDeltaNet layers, and 6 attention layers")
interface: other (precomputed BF16 weight-delta patch; column rotations on norm spheres)
loop: n/a (study protocol states up to 200 MATH-500 problems used for SGNE-CC angle selection; search not described)

headline_results.quote: the first singular mode accounts for over 99.999% of update energy. Individual column norms increase by up to 114.3%
Base solves none of the 100 problems, MIT-p50c solves 4, and SGNE-CC solves 44

headline_results.claim: Full MATH-500 under model-card settings (direct PyTorch run)
headline_results.quote: Base solves 39 problems (7.8%), MIT-p50c solves 259 (51.8%), and SGNE-CC solves 235 (47.0%; McNemar +56/−80, nominal p = 0.048)
It reaches the generation limit 17.6 times less often: 1.6% versus 28.2%.
SGNE-CC solves 24 of 49 problems while Base solves none (p = 1.19 × 10⁻⁷)
SGNE-CC solves 100 of 240 language instances (41.7%) versus 137 (57.1%) for MIT-p50c
Base passes 26 of 164 problems (15.9%), MIT-p50c passes 51 (31.1%), and SGNE-CC passes 46 (28.0%)

baselines_and_controls: Base Qwen3.5-0.8B and the MIT-p50c checkpoint; external MIT vLLM run logs as reference; two decoding regimes (greedy vs model-card sampling with presence penalty); greedy no-reasoning 4,096-token control on text generation. No random-edit or fine-tuning baseline.
runs_and_variance: "All direct PyTorch runs record one output per prompt (seed 0), so seed-to-seed variance inside the PyTorch generator is unmeasured"; exact McNemar tests and a clustered sign-flip permutation test; p-values nominal without multiplicity correction.
robustness_of_edits: Out-of-domain transfer tested (BBH-160, Web of Lies, HumanEval-164, MultiSpeech-64 in 8 languages) and decoding-regime sensitivity; not tested under fine-tuning or quantization.
verification: FP64 weight-geometry verifier script and SHA-256-locked artifacts; offline CPU verifier of trace metrics; no formal verification of behavior
memorization_vs_reasoning: n/a (no LLM editor analyzed); notes the causal role of norm preservation is not isolated: results "are consistent with this hypothesis, yet do not isolate the causal effect of norm preservation"
limitations_stated: One run per task; mixed accelerators with per-file GPU assignment not stored; nominal p-values; rotation-angle search procedure not released; freeze chronology rests on author's protocol; formal text filter does not check semantic accuracy; HumanEval grader not sandboxed.
code_or_data: https://github.com/Nondual-Observer/dna-weight-editing; Zenodo record 24235218 files (patch npz, apply script, reproducibility zip)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026, Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog; MIT-p50c edit and RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs)
notes_for_survey: Independent re-evaluation of the Sparks MIT-p50c Qwen edit: under greedy decoding without presence penalty it solves 4/100 sampled MATH-500 problems vs 45/100 with model-card sampling, i.e. its reported gain depends strongly on decoding settings. The competing SGNE-CC patch's construction method is undisclosed, so it is not attributable to any WSP editor.
